title: Ledger Repository Contract and In-memory Test Double
objective: Define and verify persistence-independent Implementation Ledger Repository behavior, typed queries, stable errors, and an in-memory test double without implementing production persistence.
scope: Synchronous Protocol contracts for Task, Run, Relationship, Detail, and aggregate Ledger repositories.
Immutable query and Page values plus stable Repository-layer errors.
Instance-local standard-library in-memory test double for identity, replay, conflict, version, cycle, query, append-only, and atomic-batch semantics.
Repository contract document, targeted tests, Project Memory updates, one immutable Implementation Run, and one local commit.
explicit_non_goals: No SQLAlchemy ORM, PostgreSQL Repository or table, quantmind2 schema, migration, Session, production Unit of Work, or database transaction implementation.
No Manifest Parser, Manifest Indexer, Git consistency service, API, or UI.
No TDX, Dataset Snapshot, Factor DSL, Optimization, Validation runtime, Registry, LightGBM, Qlib, or other research business implementation.
No Factor Lab, accepted ADR, historical Run, dependency, lockfile, runtime configuration, or secret change.
No implementation of QM2-P0-002A2 or later tasks.

known_limitations: The in-memory Repository is process-local, non-durable, and does not support multi-process or real concurrent behavior.
Expected versions validate a contract only; they are not database locks or constraints.
No database transaction, SQLAlchemy ORM, PostgreSQL table/schema, migration, Manifest Indexer, Git consistency service, API, or UI exists.
Iterative DFS cycle checks are not optimized for a large relationship graph.
Context schema v1 cannot encode exact next task QM2-P0-002A2, so machine-readable context uses parent QM2-P0-002.
ruff was unavailable and was not installed.
The containing commit cannot be embedded self-referentially; Git history resolves it after commit.
unresolved_questions: Should future Task and Run identity uniqueness be global or repository-scoped?
Which different relationship types may coexist for the same source and target pair?
How will PostgreSQL prevent relationship-cycle races under concurrency?
What canonical demotion transitions require additional authorization?
rollback_information: Revert the single containing commit. No database, migration, data, API, runtime, model, Qlib, UI, dependency, lockfile, configuration, accepted ADR, or Factor Lab rollback is required.
security_impact: Repository errors expose validated IDs rather than stored object contents; the test double performs no file, environment, network, Git, or database access.
data_lineage_impact: No research data changed; Repository contracts prepare a future derived Ledger index while Git Reports and Manifests remain authoritative.
